mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior quarter is interpreted by market participants as a signal of tightening financial conditions, which compresses equity discount rates and reduces expected future cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25 percentage points over the past quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 60-day rolling mean during high-rate regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates a labor-market dual signal of strength, which anticipates a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as investors price in sustained economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns fail to outperform the 30-day rolling average in 70% of similar labor-market strengthening episodes (rolling IC < 0.3).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% suggests accelerating consumer demand, which raises expected corporate profits and supports a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically significant versus the prior 5-day average (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% while inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 2% indicates a supply-side upturn without price pressures, which typically precedes a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns under such supply conditions are negative in > 40% of cases (rolling IC < 0.6).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the 3-month moving average of RSAFS below 350 million dollars signals a sudden contraction in bank lending, which is associated with a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as credit availability tightens.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain stable or improve during the contraction (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising job openings (HOUST) and persistent unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% indicate a labor market in transition toward balance, which often precedes a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as market uncertainty rises.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases while UNRATE remains < 4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative versus the 30-day rolling average (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the 1-month change in UNRATE below -0.2 percentage points, occurring during a period of steady FEDFUNDS at 3.5%, suggests a disinflationary trend that reduces growth expectations and drives a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly change < -0.2% while FEDFUNDS remains < 4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day rolling mean during such episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in GDPC1 (gross domestic personal consumption) of over 2% accompanied by a rise in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests a structural supply shock that reduces demand absorption capacity, leading to a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -2% while INDPRO monthly change > 1%
regime_hint: supply shock detected in consumption data
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not diverge from the 5-day rolling mean during such events (p > 0.1).
